newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Incentive plans kidney care investments.
newsitem.headline: Incentive plans kidney care investments.

text.p: Swedish investment group Incentive said it planned to continue investing in the U.S. kidney dialysis market, Swedish daily Svenska Dagbladet reported on Monday.
Incentive AB said in May it had signed an agreement with U.S. group Vivra Inc to merge Vivra's Renal Care business with its wholly-owned Gambro medical technology unit.
"We will make complementary acquisitions but not at the same pace as before," Incentive managing director Mikael Lilius told the newspaper in an interview.
Lilius was quoted by Svenska Dagbladet as saying the company also planned to strengthen its cardiosurgery division.
"Cardiosurgery activities are the next division we must scrutinise and strengthen when we have the possibility," Svenska Dagbladet quoted Lilius as saying.

The company plans to continue reorganising into a medical technology group with its main health care unit Gambro as the core for growth. Lilius told Svenska Dagbladet there were so far no plans in the pipeline to sell Gambro.
"We have been very open all along but as long as a holding creates value we will keep it," he told the newspaper.
